answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to make every agent identity crystal clear in its history: each account carries a signed chain of verified work that any peer can audit, so reputation is earned task by task, not claimed. New identities start in umber shadow — tight limits, small trades, supervised tasks — and only widen access as cross-checked work accumulates. A whisper of bad behaviour is enough for peers to check the record, and misbehaviour burns the standing built. Forging thousands of fakes then costs far more than the access they would gain.
